solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: But nettle-rash can erupt and gain the ascendancy

definitions.note: a verb phrase, matching the idiom it defines

indicators.note: to erupt is to burst out violently, so the letters of the words before it are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A nasty skin rash breaks out and gets the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is a link word; the thirteen letters of BUT NETTLE-RASH rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reverse a situation so that the former loser now has the advantage.

clue.text: News put out, with the dust allowed to settle

definitions.text: with the dust allowed to settle

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the preceding words are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A news story is released, with things left to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor never swept is one where dust has been left to lie undisturbed.

clue.text: It has a point, may need filing

definitions.meaning: a carpenter's metal spike, hammered in, has a sharp tip
the horny tip of a finger is smoothed with an emery board, which is filing it

explanation.surface: Something pointed that may have to be put in a filing cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the metal fastener with a tip and the fingertip covering one files.

clue.text: Farmers may combine to gather it in

definitions.text: Farmers may combine to gather it in

parts.words: Farmers may combine to gather it in
parts.note: combine seems to mean farmers joining forces, but it is the reaping machine farmers drive through ripe fields of grain

explanation.surface: Farmers might band together to bring in the crops.
explanation.definitionFit: The season's crop gathered from the fields is what farmers bring in each year.

clue.text: In piping form

parts.note: piping suggests music or icing, but means pipes, so the phrase describes something shaped like a tube

explanation.definitionFit: Something tube-shaped, like a length of pipe, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Display stand

definitions.meaning: to ... arms or a mark is to display or show it
to stand something is to tolerate or put up with it

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both carrying something visibly and enduring something unpleasant.

clue.text: Scholar finding sums are uplifting

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting means the words are read from the bottom up, so backwards

explanation.surface: An academic who finds that arithmetic cheers you up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns the whole of SUMS ARE: written upwards it reads ERA SMUS; 'finding' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch Renaissance humanist of Rotterdam is among history's most famous scholars.

clue.text: Conjured up nightmare of apparition

indicators.note: conjured suggests magic summoning, and here the letters that follow are magicked into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A ghostly figure summoned out of a bad dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conjured up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' belongs to the fodder: UP NIGHTMARE OF gives thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghostly shape that seems to be present but is not real is an apparition.

clue.text: One predicts there'll be a lot of money on the counter

parts.note: a fortune is a very large sum of money
a bank teller works behind the counter handling cash

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes big money on a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there'll be' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A clairvoyant who foretells the future is someone who predicts.

clue.text: Gets level, being faster

parts.note: to get something is to have it
a tier is a level, as in a tiered cake or stadium

explanation.surface: Someone draws level by speeding up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'level' tempts as 'draw level', but it is a noun giving a tier; 'being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are comparatives meaning more rapid or quicker in action.

clue.text: Boasting about a number well done

indicators.note: about means going round, so the cheer is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: bravo is the shout of praise for a fine performance
D is 500 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone brags about a job well done.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a swaggering show of boldness, close to boasting in sense.

clue.text: Born and died in poverty

parts.note: née, meaning born, introduces a woman's maiden name
d is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone who was born and died penniless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the two pieces and 'in' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Need in the sense of want or destitution is a synonym for poverty.

clue.text: He will shortly ring — to say this?

parts.note: he will shortened is the contraction he'll
the letter O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: He'll phone soon, so what will he say?
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like part of the phone call, but it gives the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the standard greeting when someone answers the telephone.

clue.text: Make an issue of time to return

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word for time is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss over a deadline to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make an issue of' suggests making a fuss, but here issue means send out.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue something in the sense of giving it out or discharging it is to emit it.

clue.text: Meat company included in embargo

indicators.note: one piece is included within the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: an embargo is an official ban on trade

explanation.surface: A meat firm caught up in a trade embargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured pork, a familiar kind of meat.

clue.text: Put on a soft layer

parts.note: p, from piano, is the musical direction for soft
a ply is a single layer, as in three-ply wool

explanation.surface: Someone spreads on a gentle coat of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To apply paint or cream is to put it on a surface.

clue.text: Stay longer than most at the wicket?

definitions.meaning: to stay on after another has gone is to last longer than them
in cricket the batter dismissed last has spent the longest at the wicket

explanation.definitionFit: To survive or endure beyond someone else is to last beyond them; the cricket reading splits the word in two.

clue.text: Pinero's play persuades one to take part

indicators.note: play suggests a drama by Pinero, but here it means the letters move loosely into a new order

explanation.surface: A play by the dramatist Pinero coaxes someone into joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Wing Pinero was a Victorian playwright; the possessive's S is a fodder letter here, giving seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to enlist or draw someone into an activity.

clue.text: Acts for different agents

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters of the words before it are given another order

explanation.surface: Someone acts on behalf of various representatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is an agent who buys and sells or manages property on another's behalf.

clue.text: Am clear out of sugar after cooking

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds they have run out of sugar once cooking is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of sugar' reads as having none left, but 'out' signals the anagram and 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Caramel is what sugar turns into when it is heated until it browns.

clue.text: Fight and give a thrashing to a tough character

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: Fighting and beating up a hard man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' joins the pieces, 'to' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spartan, after the austere ancient Greek city, is a hardy, disciplined person.

clue.text: It's forbidden, and badly one hundred may take it

parts.note: ill means badly, as in ill-treated
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A rule says a hundred people may not take something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' opens the definition as a link; 'may take' attaches the final IT to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illicit is not allowed by law or custom, so it is prohibited.

clue.text: Occupy in monastic style?

parts.note: taken as written
a habit is the robe worn by monks and nuns, so their style of dress

explanation.surface: Moving into a place the way monks would.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: monks live in habit, their robes.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit a place is to live in it or occupy it.

clue.text: Copper on trial, composed in dock

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters of the word before it are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A police officer on trial, calm in the courtroom dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'dock' both point to a courtroom, but copper is the element and dock is a verb; 'on' joins the pieces and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock wages or a tail is to cut it short, which is to curtail it.

clue.text: Returned to show off clothes

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for showing off is written backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast or show off

explanation.surface: Someone came back to flaunt their outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb is a word for clothing, especially distinctive dress.

clue.text: There's something hidden here — sounds like money

indicators.note: sounds like signals that the answer is said the same way as a word for money

parts.note: cash is money in coins and notes

explanation.surface: Someone suspects hidden treasure, the kind that sounds like money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cache is a secret store of goods or valuables hidden away.

clue.text: In for a long viva voce

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A student is in for a long spoken examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva voce is an examination conducted by speaking, so the adjective is spoken.

clue.text: Buzzer was quiet

parts.note: taken as written
p, from piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: The doorbell stayed silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A wasp is an insect that buzzes, hence a buzzer.

clue.text: The record is held by District of Columbia

indicators.note: held by means kept inside, so the short word goes within the abbreviation

parts.note: DC is the abbreviation for the District of Columbia, home of Washington

explanation.surface: The record is kept in Washington DC.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record or other recording medium.

clue.text: Batter section's defence

parts.note: a ram is a battering ram, so it batters
a part is a section; the possessive is a link

explanation.surface: The defensive role of one section of a batting line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batter' suggests a cricketer or cake mix, but it is a verb: a ram batters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive wall or bank around a fort.

clue.text: Soldiers ordered to carry equipment

indicators.note: to carry is to hold within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to order
a rig is a set of equipment, as an oil rig

explanation.surface: Troops are told to bring their kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is an army unit made up of several battalions of soldiers.

clue.text: Saucy play from which friends will return with delight

indicators.note: to return is to come back, so the word for friends is read backwards

parts.note: pals are friends
and means with, joining things together
to tickle is to amuse or delight

explanation.surface: Friends come back from somewhere pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: SLAP AND TICKLE is British slang for playful kissing and cuddling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jokey British term for amorous horseplay between lovers.
